name: foundry-packages
description: Workspace root. Not published — see packages/ for the published packages.

scripts.//shell: npm runs these with /bin/sh, which is dash on most Linux CI images and has no arrays and no shopt. They must be POSIX. An unmatched glob expands to the literal pattern, so `[ -d ]` on the first word is the portable way to ask whether packages/ has anything in it.
scripts.//build-order: npm --workspaces builds in filesystem-discovery order, not dependency order. A single layer-1-first prefix stopped being enough the moment a second package (gates) depended on something at the SAME rank as catalog (policy) but sorting after it alphabetically -- 'gates' < 'policy', so gates tried to compile against a policy dist/ that did not exist yet. Building the whole of layer 1 first, then the general pass, covers every graph shape that layer can take, because nothing in it depends on anything outside it. It stops covering the graph the moment something in layer 2 or above depends on another layer-2-or-above package -- at that point this prefix needs to become an actual call to gates' own computeBuildOrder rather than one more hand-maintained line, which needs an answer to how gates gets built before it can be used to decide build order. That bootstrap problem is deliberately not solved here.
scripts.build: set -- packages/*/; [ -d "$1" ] || exit 0; npm run build --workspace=packages/catalog --if-present && npm run build --workspace=packages/policy --if-present && npm run build --workspaces --if-present
scripts.test: set -- packages/*/; [ -d "$1" ] || exit 0; npm run test --workspaces --if-present
scripts.typecheck: set -- packages/*/; [ -d "$1" ] || exit 0; npm run typecheck --workspaces --if-present
scripts.check:readme: node scripts/check-root-readme-parity.mjs . && for p in packages/*/; do [ -d "$p" ] || continue; node scripts/check-readme-parity.mjs "$p" || exit 1; done
scripts.check:contamination: for p in packages/*/; do [ -d "$p" ] || continue; node scripts/check-contamination-classes.mjs "$p" || exit 1; done
scripts.check:typechecked-assertions: for p in packages/*/; do [ -d "$p" ] || continue; node scripts/check-typechecked-assertions.mjs "$p" || exit 1; done
scripts.//check-builds-first: build runs before typecheck for the same reason ci.yml does it in that order: dist/ is gitignored, so on a fresh clone a package's internal dependency has no .d.ts until it has been compiled. Without this a contributor's first `npm run check` fails on a clean checkout even though nothing is wrong.
scripts.check: npm run check:scope && npm run check:gates && npm run check:safety && npm run check:readme && npm run check:contamination && npm run check:typechecked-assertions && npm run build && npm run typecheck && npm run test
scripts.//preflight: Everything a package must pass before a publish is even proposed. Unlike `check`, this scans the packed TARBALL and asks the registry whether the name is already taken.
